clue.text: Stamp shows this person's reversed head

indicators.note: reversed tells us the word for this person is to be written backwards

parts.note: this person, said by the setter, is me
a boss is the head of an organisation

explanation.surface: A stamp depicts the speaker's own head shown back to front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversed' applies only to the word for this person; 'head' is a boss, not a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: To emboss is to stamp a raised design onto a surface, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Scotsman heading off in smart footwear

indicators.note: in places the shortened Scotsman inside the word for smart

parts.note: to smart is to sting with pain

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter of the Scotsman word is dropped

parts.note: Jock is a familiar nickname for a Scotsman

explanation.surface: A Scotsman sets off wearing his best shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' removes the J from JOCK, leaving OCK, which goes 'in' STING.
explanation.definitionFit: A stocking is a close-fitting garment worn on the foot and leg, a kind of hosiery.

clue.text: Woman graduate curious about one collection of plants

parts.note: her is a pronoun for a woman
BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate

indicators.note: about means the word for curious goes round the letter for one

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or curious
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A female graduate is oddly interested in a set of plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals that the numeral for one sits inside the word for curious; 'rum' meaning odd is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A herbarium is a systematic collection of dried, preserved plant specimens.

clue.text: Men on bunk: one turns round

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another means it comes after it

parts.note: bunk and rot both mean nonsense
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers or men

explanation.surface: Soldiers lying on their bunks, one rolling over.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotor is the rotating part of a machine, such as a helicopter's blades.

clue.text: Expecting complex start to exam, why many fail it

indicators.note: complex here signals that the letters are tangled together into a new order
start to selects the opening letter of exam

explanation.surface: An exam so difficult that many fail it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start to exam' gives E; 'complex' rearranges E with WHY MANY FAIL IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the family way is an informal idiom for pregnancy, just as expecting is.

clue.text: Tie horses here

definitions.meaning: a broad cravat or neck tie
A famous English racecourse in Berkshire where horses race

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a wide neckcloth and the Berkshire racecourse, hence both senses.

clue.text: Speaking formally, I'm boring one country or another

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: India is one country
a formal speaker says one's (one is) in place of I'm

explanation.surface: Speaking stiffly, I am tedious about one nation or another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' wants to mean dull, but it is the container; 'or another' points the definition at a second country.
explanation.definitionFit: Indonesia is a second nation in Asia, distinct from India, so it is another country.

clue.text: Nudity in California, perhaps, could make her — unemployed?

definitions.text: Nudity in California, perhaps, could make her — unemployed?

parts.note: LA, Los Angeles, is an example of a place in California
undress is a state of having no clothes on

explanation.surface: If everyone in California went naked, a washerwoman would be out of a job.
explanation.walkthrough: LA followed by UNDRESS; the whole clue describes her: with no clothes to wash, a laundress has no work.
explanation.definitionFit: A laundress is a woman who washes clothes, and nudity would leave her without work.

clue.text: Macho assassin dispatching Queen

indicators.note: dispatching means sending away, so the Queen's letters are removed

parts.note: a butcher is a brutal killer
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A tough killer bumps off the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dispatching' removes ER from BUTCHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Butch is an informal adjective for aggressively masculine, a synonym for macho.

clue.text: Dire telegram is scrambled for guaranteed delivery

indicators.note: scrambled means jumbled, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: An alarming telegram is garbled despite being sent securely.
explanation.definitionFit: Registered mail is a postal service that records and assures the arrival of an item.

clue.text: Landowner set out across river

indicators.note: across means the phrase for set out spans the letter for river

parts.note: laid out and set out both mean arranged

explanation.surface: A property owner sets off over a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: LAID goes 'across' R, giving LAI-R-D.
explanation.definitionFit: A laird is a Scottish term for a landed proprietor owning an estate.

clue.text: Likely voting system modified, Conservative admitted

parts.note: PR is proportional representation, a voting system

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so one letter goes inside the word for modified

parts.note: edited means altered or modified

explanation.surface: A voting system is probably changed with a Tory let in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitted' signals that the Conservative letter is let inside the word for modified; PR is a common crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Something predicted is expected or forecast to happen, i.e. probable.

clue.text: Prior to bow before southern clergy

parts.note: pre is a prefix meaning before or prior to
to bow is to bend

explanation.surface: Bowing first before the clergymen of the south.
explanation.definitionFit: Prebends are the stipends of cathedral canons, and by extension the canons who hold them.

clue.text: Settle return of most of fee in court

indicators.note: return of tells us the whole construction is written backwards
in places the shortened fee inside the word for court

parts.note: a yard is an enclosed courtyard

indicators.note: most of means the last letter of fee is dropped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Settling a refund of most of a charge in a law court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims FEE to FE, put 'in' YARD to give YARFED; 'return of' turns that into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To defray costs is to pay them, so it means settle a bill.

clue.text: Rocky hit cleanly, according to his custom?

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady or shaky, signalling a rearrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A boxer called Rocky landing a clean punch, as his people's custom dictates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocky' looks like a name, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting by one's people's customs is behaving according to ethnic tradition.

clue.text: Subjected to fire, Navy in unwieldy boat capsized

indicators.note: in places the navy letters inside the upturned boat
capsized means turned over, so the boat word is read upwards in this down clue

parts.note: a tub is a clumsy, slow boat
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A naval vessel, clumsy and overturned, is under fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capsized' turns TUB into BUT, and RN goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something burnt has been damaged by being exposed to fire.

clue.text: Most hackneyed stories, in a way

indicators.note: in places the stories inside the abbreviation for a way

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
tales are stories

explanation.surface: The most worn-out stories, told in one manner.
explanation.walkthrough: TALES goes 'in' ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalest is the superlative of stale, meaning most trite or overused.

clue.text: No good ducking casual employment rates

indicators.note: ducking means dodging, so the letters for no good drop out

parts.note: temping is temporary office work

explanation.surface: Avoiding a worthless temporary job at low pay rates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ducking' removes NG from TEMPING.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempi is the plural of tempo, the speed or rate at which music is played.

clue.text: Wage racket

definitions.meaning: to wage war is to conduct or continue it
a racket here is a noisy fuss or commotion

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the phrase means continue or conduct; as a noun it is British slang for a fuss.

clue.text: Broken-down train isn't on the way

indicators.note: broken-down means wrecked, so the letters are rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: A train that has broken down is not coming.
explanation.definitionFit: In transit is an idiom for being carried along a route towards a destination.

clue.text: Bound horse kicked off saddle strap

indicators.note: kicked off means thrown out, so the letter for horse is removed

parts.note: a girth is the strap holding a saddle on a horse
horse is slang for heroin, whose abbreviation is H

explanation.surface: A tied-up horse has thrown off its saddle strap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kicked off' removes H from GIRTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Girt is an archaic past participle of gird, meaning encircled or tied.

clue.text: A means of stabilising vehicle that's drawn up in late afternoon?

indicators.note: in places the upturned vehicle inside the late afternoon hour

parts.note: five o'clock is late afternoon

indicators.note: drawn up in a down clue means written from bottom to top

parts.note: a taxi is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A steadying thing: a car pulled up at teatime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's drawn up' turns TAXI into IXAT, which goes 'in' FIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixative is a substance used to fix or preserve something, such as a drawing or specimen.

clue.text: Leave at end of test, when official concessions are made

indicators.note: at end of means the leave piece comes after the test piece

parts.note: to tax is to strain or test
a holiday is leave from work

explanation.surface: Going on holiday once the exam is over.
explanation.definitionFit: A tax holiday is a period during which a government suspends taxes as an incentive.

clue.text: Doctor short of time tries acute move to stop infection

indicators.note: move means shift around, so the remaining letters are rearranged
short of means lacking, so the letter for time is removed

explanation.surface: A doctor in a hurry makes a sharp intervention against infection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short of time' removes one T from TRIES ACUTE; 'move' rearranges the rest. 'to stop infection' completes the sense of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To cauterise is to treat a wound by burning, a medical procedure to prevent infection.

clue.text: Demobbed South Africa marine's stopped going outside

indicators.note: outside means the word for stopped going wraps around the other letters

parts.note: died means stopped working, as an engine does
RM stands for Royal Marine

explanation.surface: A South African marine has stopped serving, now demobilised.
explanation.walkthrough: DIED goes 'outside' SA and RM.
explanation.definitionFit: Demobbed troops have been stood down and so no longer bear arms.

clue.text: Woodwind leader secures contract

indicators.note: secures means holds within, so the letters are concealed inside these words

explanation.surface: The principal of the woodwind section signs a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwindle is to shrink or diminish, which is what contract means as a verb.

clue.text: Establish what's to be served when one's due for retirement?

parts.note: to bed in is to establish or settle firmly
a prisoner serves time

explanation.surface: Settling the length of a prison sentence before one retires from work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' looks like leaving work, but here it is going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Retiring for the night means going to bed, which happens at a set hour.

clue.text: Half-hearted council's back, retaining power

indicators.note: retaining means holding inside, so the letter for power is kept within
back means the council word is read in reverse

parts.note: a diet is a legislative assembly or council

explanation.surface: A lukewarm council holds on to power behind the scenes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns DIET into TEID, 'retaining' P inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tepid means lukewarm, and figuratively unenthusiastic.

clue.text: Moving melody holy man's penned

indicators.note: penned means shut in, so the saint's letters go inside the melody

parts.note: an air is a tune or melody
ST is the abbreviation for saint, a holy man

explanation.surface: A stirring tune written by a holy man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned' looks like written, but here it means enclosed, as animals are penned.
explanation.definitionFit: Astir means up and about, in motion or activity.

clue.text: Served up beer in error

indicators.note: served up in a down clue means the beer word is written upwards

parts.note: pils is a pilsner beer

explanation.surface: A drink handed out by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Served up' turns PILS upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip is a small mistake or lapse.
